content.topic: Pulmonary embolism (PE) — research and practice gaps / recommendations

points: Need to assess RV (right ventricular) status in addition to clinical parameters to classify acute symptomatic PE as low vs. intermediate risk; requires confirmation in prospective cohort studies.
Clinical benefits vs. risks of reduced-dose thrombolysis and catheter-based reperfusion in intermediate–high-risk PE should be evaluated in prospective randomized trials.
Role of ECMO in management of acute high-risk PE requires additional evidence from prospective cohort studies.
Optimal anticoagulant drug(s) and regimens for patients with renal insufficiency (CrCl < 30 mL/min) remain unclear.

Criteria for selecting patients for early discharge and outpatient treatment of PE — including assessment of RV status with imaging and laboratory markers alongside clinical scores — need validation in prospective cohort studies.

key_points.section: Chronic treatment and prevention of recurrence
points: Clinical value and therapeutic implications of models/scores assessing VTE recurrence risk and bleeding risk under anticoagulation need re-evaluation in the NOAC era.
Effectiveness of extended treatment with reduced dose, or with apixaban or rivaroxaban, should be confirmed in patients at high risk of recurrent PE.
Evidence supporting efficacy and safety of NOACs for treatment of PE in patients with cancer needs further studies.
In cancer patients, the anticoagulant regimen and dose after the first 6 months should be clarified and prospectively tested.
Optimal time for discontinuing anticoagulant treatment after an acute PE in cancer patients is undetermined.
Diagnostic algorithms for PE in pregnancy using modern radiological techniques and low radiation doses need prospective testing in adequately powered cohort studies.
Controversy persists regarding optimal LMWH dose and regimen for treatment of PE during pregnancy.
NOACs are not allowed in pregnancy; if exposure occurs despite warnings, possible effects on the fetus should be recorded to provide more precise data.

uncertainties_requiring_research: Validation of RV assessment in risk classification
Prospective randomized trials for reduced-dose thrombolysis and catheter-based reperfusion
Evidence for ECMO use in high-risk PE
Optimal anticoagulant choice/regimen in renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min)
Long-term anticoagulation strategies and dosing in cancer-associated PE
Safe diagnostic and treatment protocols for PE in pregnancy
